```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML, display

DATA_PATH = Path("motorcycle_accidents_colombia.csv")
data = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

required = {
    "date_of_death",
    "gender",
    "age group",
    "department of residence",
    "municipality_of_residence",
    "condition",
}
missing = required.difference(data.columns)
if missing:
    raise ValueError(f"CSV is missing required columns: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")

data["date_of_death"] = pd.to_datetime(data["date_of_death"], errors="coerce", utc=True)
total = len(data)
if not total:
    raise ValueError("The CSV contains no records.")

antioquia_count = data["department of residence"].str.casefold().eq("antioquia").sum()
medellin_count = data["municipality_of_residence"].str.casefold().eq("medellín").sum()
age_20_24_count = data["age group"].eq("20-24").sum()
age_20_34_count = data["age group"].isin(["20-24", "25-29", "30-34"]).sum()
valid_dates = data["date_of_death"].dropna()
if valid_dates.empty:
    raise ValueError("No valid date_of_death values are available.")
period = f"{valid_dates.min():%Y-%m-%d} to {valid_dates.max():%Y-%m-%d}"

municipality_counts = (
    data.loc[
        data["municipality_of_residence"].str.casefold().ne("unknown"),
        "municipality_of_residence",
    ]
    .value_counts()
    .head(8)
    .sort_values()
)
age_gender_counts = pd.crosstab(data["age group"], data["gender"])
age_order = sorted(
    age_gender_counts.index,
    key=lambda band: int(str(band).split("-")[0]) if str(band).split("-")[0].isdigit() else 999,
)
age_gender_counts = age_gender_counts.reindex(age_order)
yearly_counts = valid_dates.dt.year.value_counts().sort_index()

display(
    HTML(
        f"""
        <div class="kpi-grid">
          <div class="kpi"><span class="kpi-value">{total:,}</span><span class="kpi-label">Person records in file</span></div>
          <div class="kpi"><span class="kpi-value">{medellin_count / total:.1%}</span><span class="kpi-label">List Medellín as residence</span></div>
          <div class="kpi"><span class="kpi-value">{age_20_24_count / total:.1%}</span><span class="kpi-label">Aged 20–24</span></div>
        </div>
        """
    )
)
```

> **INSIGHT** · Ages 20–34 account for **{age_20_34_count:,} of {total:,} records ({age_20_34_count / total:.1%})**. Antioquia is the listed department of residence for **{antioquia_count:,} records ({antioquia_count / total:.1%})**.

The supplied file describes **person records**, not all reported crash incidents. Residence is not necessarily crash location, and the dataset has no injury-severity field.

## What the records show

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.1))
municipality_counts.plot(kind="barh", ax=ax, color="#2878b5", width=0.68)
ax.set_title("Records by municipality of residence", loc="left", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", color="#16263d")
ax.set_xlabel("Person records in supplied file")
ax.set_ylabel("")
ax.grid(axis="x", color="#dce4ef")
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#dce4ef")
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
ax.set_xlim(0, municipality_counts.max() * 1.18)
for y, value in enumerate(municipality_counts.values):
    ax.text(value + municipality_counts.max() * 0.015, y, f"{value:,}", va="center", fontsize=9, color="#16263d")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Medellín is the most frequently listed municipality of residence (**{medellin_count:,} records**). This cannot be interpreted as a count of crashes occurring in Medellín.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2))
age_gender_counts.plot(
    kind="bar",
    stacked=True,
    ax=ax,
    color=["#e69b37" if str(gender).casefold() == "female" else "#2878b5" for gender in age_gender_counts.columns],
    width=0.72,
)
ax.set_title("Records by age group and gender", loc="left", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", color="#16263d")
ax.set_xlabel("Age group")
ax.set_ylabel("Person records in supplied file")
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#dce4ef")
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color("#dce4ef")
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#dce4ef")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=40)
ax.legend(title="Gender", frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The 20–24 group is the largest single age band (**{age_20_24_count:,} records**). Counts and group shares describe only the supplied file; without population or travel-exposure denominators, they do not compare risk.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.4))
yearly_counts.plot(kind="bar", ax=ax, color="#12a594", width=0.58)
ax.set_title("Records by year of death", loc="left", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", color="#16263d")
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Person records in supplied file")
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#dce4ef")
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color("#dce4ef")
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#dce4ef")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=0)
for x, value in enumerate(yearly_counts.values):
    ax.text(x, value + yearly_counts.max() * 0.02, f"{value}", ha="center", fontsize=9, color="#16263d")
ax.set_ylim(0, yearly_counts.max() * 1.14)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Dates in this file are **dates of death**, covering **{period}**. They are not crash dates or times, so the annual counts are not a crash trend.

## Data, tool, and interpretation

- **Tool:** Python, pandas, Matplotlib, and Quarto.
- **Dataset:** `motorcycle_accidents_colombia.csv`, the file supplied with this project. The upstream publisher/URL was not included.
- **Reporting period:** {period}, calculated from valid `date_of_death` values.
- **Caution:** The file has no crash-site location, incident identifier, non-fatal records, explicit severity measure, or exposure denominator. It cannot answer where crashes occurred or how crash severity varies. The reported counts are not measures of underlying road-safety risk.

To answer the original crash-location and severity question, obtain incident-level data with crash coordinates/location, crash date, explicit injury outcome categories, coverage information, and suitable exposure denominators.
